title: Online Assessment Platforms (TCS iON, AMCAT)
tagline: Year 4 — How timed online tests behave: timers, navigation, review marks, auto-submit and what to check in the official demo

introduction.overview: Employers commonly use third-party online platforms (TCS iON and AMCAT are two well-known names) to run aptitude tests. Each platform has its own interface and each employer configures its own rules, so this chapter does not describe any platform's specific pattern. It teaches what features to look for in an official demo or instruction page: whether the timer is sectional or overall, whether you can go back, whether answers can be marked for review, what happens at time-out, and how the calculator or rough work is handled. All figures and rules in this chapter's examples are hypothetical teaching examples and are not the rules of any real company or platform; always read the official instructions.
introduction.placementRelevance: Familiarity with the interface removes avoidable errors and saves seconds on every question.
introduction.realWorldContext: Any new software is easier if you read its documentation and try a demo first.

learningObjectives: List the features to verify in an official demo
Plan around sectional versus overall timers
Prepare the device and connection in advance

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: The pattern and interface are set by the employer and platform; the official instructions override anything you have heard.

coreDefinitions: Sectional timer: each section has its own clock.
Overall timer: one clock for the whole test.
Mark for review: a flag to revisit a question.
Auto-submit: the test ends when time runs out.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: An interface is a set of rules about time and navigation; know them and you stop fighting the tool.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Before the test: take the official demo, note timer type, navigation and what the review flag does.

mainNarrative: Suppose the (hypothetical) rules say: overall timer of 45 minutes, free navigation, review flag allowed, auto-submit at time-out. With free navigation you can follow a two-pass plan and use the last 5 minutes for flagged questions.
If the timer is sectional with no return, plan each section as a closed block and do not leave time for review in other sections.
If an on-screen calculator is provided, practise with it; if not, practise rough work on paper.
Check your device, power and network the day before and keep the instructions page open to read the official rules.
Whatever the platform, follow the exact instructions on the day.
